chunks: Then He gave Adam knowledge of the nature and reality of all things and everything, and set them before the angels and said: "Tell Me the names of these if you are truthful."

key_terms.آدَمَ: Adam, the first human and prophet.
key_terms.أَنْبِئُونِي: Inform me; a command to report or declare knowledge.
key_terms.الْأَسْمَاءَ: The names; refers to the names of all things, signifying comprehensive knowledge or the faculty of naming/defining.
key_terms.صَادِقِينَ: Truthful; confirming the accuracy of their report.

ai.seo_question: What does the phrase 'He taught Adam the names' mean in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'al-asma' (the names) is often interpreted as the Divine Names and Attributes, signifying Adam's possession of comprehensive metaphysical knowledge (ilm al-asma) that distinguishes him from the angels. This event serves as the foundational proof for Adam's vicegerency (khilafah), demonstrating that his capacity to comprehend and articulate divine realities surpasses the angelic realm, thereby justifying his role as the first Imam and Prophet.
